entry.title: Understanding How Containers Communicate in Docker and Kubernetes
entry.summary: A beginner-friendly guide to Docker networking When you run an application in Docker, it doesn't automatically know how to reach other services. A container is isolated by default — it has its own network namespace, its own IP address, and its own view of the world. For two services to talk, you have to explicitly connect them. This is something I learned while building SwiftDeploy. My Go API and Nginx were in separate containers and I didn't have full understanding of ow they communicated with each other. This is the most common scenario — an API and a database, or a frontend and a backend. The wrong way is to use localhost. If your API tries to connect to localhost:5432 for PostgreSQL, it won't work. Inside a container, localhost refers to the container itself — not your host machine, no…

entry.title: Chinese LLMs Are Ridiculously Cheap — Why Aren't More Developers Using Them?
entry.summary:
I've been experimenting with Chinese LLMs recently and the pricing caught me off guard:
Model Input (per 1M tokens) Output (per 1M tokens)
GPT-4o $2.50 $10.00
DeepSeek V4 $0.30 $0.50
Qwen3.5-Plus $0.11 $0.67
Qwen-Long $0.07 $0.28
That's 8-20x cheaper than GPT-4o depending on the model. From my experience, the main barriers for non-Chinese developers are: Payment — Most providers only accept Alipay/WeChat Pay Documentation — English docs are limited or missing API compatibility — Each provider has its own format Trust — Concerns about data handling and compliance I've been running side-by-side tests. For general tasks (chat, summarization, code assistance), DeepSeek and Qwen hold up surprisingly well. They're not beating GPT-4o on everything, but for the price? Hard to ignore. For those of you who have tried Chinese LLMs — what was your experience? And for those who haven't, what's holding you back? Would love to hear different perspectives in the comments.
